display.purpose: Hero statements only — one per page. Source Serif 4 carries the institutional voice.

body.purpose: All running text in Inter; 65–75ch max line length.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover state of interactive cards; never at rest (The Flat-At-Rest Rule).

shadows.name: hover-raise
shadows.purpose: Stronger lift for featured interactive elements.

motion.name: ease-out-standard
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out for state transitions; no bounce, no elastic.

components.name: Primary Button

narrative.overview: Tuma is a financial record you can see straight through: everything visible, permanent, precise. The interface carries the quiet assurance of a serious banking app — confident, precise, calm — while its single promise (every shilling provable) shapes every visual decision. Light, airy slate surfaces read like a clean page of accounts; Harbor Teal marks the institution's voice; proof elements are always one click away and visually privileged when they appear.
keyCharacteristics: Light, spacious, ledger-clean surfaces with generous whitespace
One institutional color (Harbor Teal) used with restraint
Serif display voice over a working sans body
Flat at rest; depth appears only as a response to state
Proof and verification elements treated as first-class UI citizens

rules.name: The One Coral Rule
rules.body: Signal Coral touches at most ~5% of any screen. Its rarity is what makes it warm instead of alarming. If coral appears twice in one viewport, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Cool Page Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds stay in the cool slate family. Warm/cream/beige page backgrounds are prohibited — warmth comes from coral, imagery, and copy, never from the canvas.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 speaks only in headings (h1–h4). Everything that works — body, labels, buttons, data — is Inter. A serif below 1.5rem is a mistake.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: No surface carries a shadow while idle. If a card is not interactive, it never gets one at all.

dos: Do use theme tokens for every color; hard-coded hex in components is prohibited.
Do hold body text at ≥4.5:1 contrast; Slate Mist (#64748b) is the lightest allowed text color on light surfaces.
Do provide a reduced-motion alternative for every animation (prefers-reduced-motion).
Do build every button, form, and table from the shared components — one source of truth per primitive.
Do treat loading (skeletons), empty, and error states as designed states, not afterthoughts.
donts: Don't ship the charity-website cliché: no sad-imagery guilt appeals, no hand-heart icons, no template NGO layouts.
Don't ship crypto/web3 aesthetics: no dark neon gradients, no coin imagery, no wallet-speak — blockchain stays invisible, verification stays visible.
Don't ship corporate bank stiffness or the university-project look (default template spacing, stock layouts, inconsistent components).
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, side-stripe borders (border-left accents), or nested cards. Ever.
Don't put Signal Coral on primary actions or use it twice in one viewport (The One Coral Rule).
Don't warm the canvas: no cream, sand, or beige backgrounds (The Cool Page Rule).
Don't apply urgency mechanics — countdowns, guilt pressure, artificial scarcity. Calm confidence, not charity urgency.
